title: Psychology
tagline: How the science of the mind emerged.
source: Generated from “Timeline of psychology” on Wikipedia; each event links to its source article.

events.title: Ebers Papyrus
events.text: The Ebers Papyrus mentioned depression and thought disorders.

events.title: Oribasius
events.text: Oribasius compiled medical writings based on the works of Aristotle, Asclepiades, and Soranus of Ephesus, and wrote on melancholia in Galenic terms.

events.title: Ali ibn Sahl Rabban al-Tabari
events.text: Ali ibn Sahl Rabban al-Tabari wrote a work emphasizing the need for psychotherapy.

events.title: Marsilio Ficino
events.text: 1499 Marsilio Ficino was a renowned figure of the Italian Renaissance, a Neoplatonist humanist, a translator of Greek philosophical writing, and the most influential exponent of Platonism in Italy in the fifteenth century.

events.title: Johann Christian Reil
events.text: Johann Christian Reil coined the term "psychiatry".

events.title: University of Leipzig
events.text: Wilhelm Wundt opened the first experimental psychology laboratory at the University of Leipzig in Germany.

events.title: Society for Psychical Research
events.text: The Society for Psychical Research was founded in England.

events.title: James Mark Baldwin
events.text: James Mark Baldwin founded the first permanent experimental psychology laboratory in the British Empire at the University of Toronto.

events.title: Sigmund Freud
events.text: Sigmund Freud published The Psychopathology of Everyday Life.

events.title: Boris Sidis
events.text: Boris Sidis published Nervous Ills: Their Cause and a Cure, a popularization of his work concerning the subconscious and the treatment of psychopathic disease.

references.label: Nervous Ills: Their Cause and a Cure

events.title: Clark L. Hull
events.text: Clark L. Hull published Hypnosis and Suggestibility, proving that hypnosis is not sleep and founding the modern study of hypnosis.

events.title: Pyotr Gannushkin
events.text: Pyotr Gannushkin published Manifestations of Psychopathies.

events.title: Stanley Smith Stevens
events.text: Stanley Smith Stevens published his levels of measurement theory.

events.title: Harry Stack Sullivan
events.text: Harry Stack Sullivan published The Interpersonal Theory of Psychiatry, which holds that an individual's personality is formed by relationships.

events.title: Rollo May
events.text: Rollo May published The Meaning of Anxiety.

events.title: Jean M. Mandler
events.text: Jean M. Mandler and George Mandler published Thinking: From Association to Gestalt.

events.title: Thomas Szasz
events.text: Thomas Szasz inaugurated the anti-psychiatry movement with the publication of his book, The Myth of Mental Illness.

events.title: E.O. Wilson
events.text: E.O. Wilson published On Human Nature, considered the first landmark text to deal with what would become evolutionary psychology.

events.title: Paul Ekman
events.text: Paul Ekman published the Facial Action Coding System.

events.title: Sex Roles
events.text: The journal Sex Roles was founded.

events.title: Erik Erikson
events.text: Erik Erikson published The Life Cycle Completed, expanding on Erikson's stages of psychosocial development.

events.title: magical thinking
events.text: A study reports that magical thinking emerges more frequently under high-stress (e.g. immediate death anxiety) conditions.

events.title: American Psychoanalytic Association
events.text: The American Psychoanalytic Association (APsaA) passed a resolution opposing "public or private discrimination" against homosexuals. It stopped short, however, of agreeing to open its training institutes to these individuals.

events.title: pandemic COVID-19
events.text: 2020s – The pandemic COVID-19 and its mitigation have a substantiall toll on mental health worldwide.

events.title: climate change
events.text: With growing awareness and impacts of climate change and other environmental issues, ecopsychology increasingly gathers public attention and becomes a more common topic of research
